title: Smoother admittance probe journal (field notes)
content:
Field journal: Smoother admittance probe
Owner: Odette Park (eng-serving-runtime) — scratchpad for evening runs
Collaborators: Maya Li (telemetry), Ravi Patel (batching)

Goal / quick hypothesis:
- Test whether a small moving-average-based admittance window ("smoother") reduces p99 tail amplification during short 5–30s surge pulses without harming p50 or sustained throughput.
- Hypothesis: smoothing admission decisions over a 3–6s horizon will prevent aggressive admission oscillation on cold-paths and reduce tail due to repeated preemption/warmup cycles.

Why this matters right now:
- On customer demo cluster we saw repeated p99 spikes during demo replay of client traffic with frequent short bursts (5-12s). The runtime was oscillating between admit/hold for cold tokens; warm cache didn't stabilize quickly.

Experiment setup (cluster snapshot):
- Model: opt-6.7b-quant (config: int8, kvcache enabled)
- Fleet: 4 x A100-40GB (dedicated test pool), driver commit: runtime@a9f7c1 (PR 789), linux kernel 6.1.0
- Traffic generator: synthetic replay of production ingress (zipf alpha=1.2) with injected burst pulses (pulse lengths: 5s, 12s, 30s) spaced by 60s quiet windows.
- Client mix: 70% text-generation (seq len avg 120), 30% embeddings (short).
- Admission baseline: immediate admission + preemptive-evict warmup policy (current prod-like).
- Smoother variants: 
  * S0 (baseline): no smoother
  * S1: exp-moving-average (alpha=0.5) on admission score, window ~2s equivalent
  * S2: simple moving-average over 3s (sliding window), weighted recent=1
  * S3: moving-average over 6s with hysteresis (require 2 consecutive admits after hold)
- Each run: 20 minute total, 10 burst pulses per run for 5s/12s case, 6 pulses for 30s case. 3 repeats per variant.

Metrics collected:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 service latency (generation path)
- end-to-end tail due to warmup (time from request arrival to first token generation)
- admission change rate (changes/sec), warm cache hit ratio, KV cache priming time, throughput (inferred RPS)
- per-run cost estimate (tokens*gpu_time) — rough

Raw observations (selected runs) — run timestamps in UTC:
- Run A (S0 baseline, 2025-11-03T02:14:00Z): typical p50=34ms, p95=220ms, p99=760ms during 5s pulses; admission-change-rate=4.2/s; warm-prime spikes correlated with p99 spikes (see telemetry).
- Run B (S2, 2025-11-03T03:02:00Z): p50=36ms, p95=190ms, p99=410ms during same pulses; admission-change-rate=1.1/s; cache priming smoother, warm-cache hit ratio +8pp.
- Run C (S3, 2025-11-03T04:10:00Z, 30s pulses): p50=38ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms; throughput slightly lower (~-3% avg) but tail much tighter vs baseline where p99 hit 1.2s in some spikes.

Quick ascii-ish chart (p99 vs pulse length, aggregated)
- Pulse 5s: S0=760ms | S1=540ms | S2=410ms | S3=430ms
- Pulse 12s: S0=920ms | S1=610ms | S2=480ms | S3=470ms
- Pulse 30s: S0=1.2s  | S1=730ms | S2=490ms | S3=480ms

Notes / interpretation:
- S2 (3s moving average) consistently reduces p99 by ~40–55% for short pulses with negligible p50 regression. It reduced admission flip-rate significantly which matches the intuition: reducing oscillation reduces repeated expensive cache loads and preemptions.
- S1 (EMA alpha=0.5) helps but not as stable as S2 — sensitive to alpha tuning.
- S3 (6s + hysteresis) kept tail low but introduced slight throughput drop during longer sustained pulses; admission hysteresis occasionally delayed full admit when it would have been safe, causing small throughput loss.

Tradeoffs observed:
- Strong smoothing reduces tail but can increase latency for the very first requests when the smoother is cold (corner-case): a 20–50ms extra for first 1–2 requests per cluster node. This is small compared to p99 improvement but worth noting for micro-bench SLAs.
- Hysteresis prevents flip-flopping but risks underutilization under gradual ramps. Might be OK for bursty patterns but not for slow ramps.

Telemetry snippets (interesting counters):
- Admission-change-rate (baseline): mean 4.2/s, max 12/s during 5s bursts
- Admission-change-rate (S2): mean 1.1/s, max 2.6/s
- Warm-priming-events/sec baseline: 0.8 -> S2: 0.25 (reduction ~69%)
- KV cache prefill time median: baseline 120ms -> S2 48ms (priming amortized across fewer churn events)

Immediate action items (short):
1) Propose S2 as a default "soft smoother" in the admission controller behind a flag for Canary (dedicated test pool). Write PR with toggles and metrics gate (owner: me).
2) Instrument additional gauge: "admit-window-age" so we can correlate smoother lag vs first-token penalty in more detail (owner: Maya).
3) Run longer 4h soak with client-mix variations (more embeddings-heavy) to see throughput impact (owner: Ravi).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How does smoother interact with preemptive-evict vs preemptive-warm policies? From quick runs it looks complementary but need a matrix of combos.
- Edge-case: repeated tiny spikes (0.5–2s). S2 window might be too long; consider adaptive window (shorten when spike energy low).
- Multi-tenant fairness: smoothing admission at a node level could bias cold-tenant requests under high contention. Need tenancy-aware smoothing or per-tenant windows in the admission controller.

PR notes / implementation considerations:
- Keep the smoother implementation lock-free and cheap: maintain a rolling sum + count for moving average, window bucketed into 250ms buckets to avoid per-request overhead.
- Add metrics: smoother_window_seconds, smoother_active (bool), smoother_flip_count, smoother_first_token_penalty_ms.
- Feature flag with rollout percentage and auto-roll back on p99>threshold.

Personal retrospective (notes-to-self):
- Loved how telemetry made the story clear — warm-priming events dropped and p99 followed. Good example of connecting low-level cache noise to user-visible SLA.
- Keep S2 tuned conservative (3s) as default; avoid hysteresis in first canary pass.

References / links:
- INF-4823 (admittance smoothing spike mitigation) — prototype design in ticket
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (contains prototype and harness)
- Slack log: #runtime-bench thread (ts:1709500000.000200) — raw run notes and telemetry traces attached

End of journal entry. Will iterate after long-soak & multi-tenant matrix.

-- Odette
